_note: Five days of daily practice for each lesson in the reading sequence, across the five mClass measures: oral reading fluency and accuracy from the lesson's own decodable passage (the same passage all week, because repeated reading is what moves those two), word reading and letter sounds from different words each day, and a maze whose blanks shift daily over the same text. Generated by scripts/build-daily-practice.mjs; do not hand-edit.

passage.title: Nat and the Map
paras: Nat is a cat. Nat has a tan hat. The hat is not big. It is a cat hat.
Dad sat on a mat. Dad had a map. The map was for a run up to see Nan.
Nat ran at the map. Nat sat on it. “Get up, Nat,” said Dad. Nat did not get up.
Dad put the map on his lap. Nat sat on the lap. Nat had a nap on Dad.
Dad can see the map now. Nat can nap. Dad and Nat are pals.

lessons.name: Short vowel review (i, o, u, e)

passage.title: The Pig in the Pen
paras: Rob has a pig. The pig is big. Rob put the pig in a pen.
The pig did not sit. He dug in the mud. He dug a pit by the log.
Then the pig was out. He ran in the sun. He sat in the wet mud and did not get up.
Rob ran to get him. The pig ran too. Rob sat down in the mud.
Now Rob is wet. The pig is wet. Rob did not get mad. He let the pig sit in the mud.

passage.title: Go, Bo, Go
paras: Bo is my pup. Bo is red. He can go and go and go.
We go up to the top of the lot. Bo digs. He digs a pit by a log.
I say, “No, Bo. We can not dig a pit by the log.”
Bo sits. He is sad. So I give him a pat. He is not sad a lot.
We go to the van. Bo is on my lap. He is my pup and I am his.

passage.title: The Red Hen
paras: Peg has a hen. The hen is red. Peg put the hen in a pen.
The hen got out. It ran to the mud by the tub. It did not go in the pen.
Peg got a bit of a bun. She put the bit in the pen.
The hen ran in to get the bun. Peg got the pen set.
Now the hen is in the pen. Peg is not mad. She is a bit wet, but the hen is in.

passage.title: Jack the Duck
paras: Nick has a duck. The duck is Jack. Jack sits on a rock in the sun.
Jack will not get up. Nick can not get him up. Jack just sits.
Nick picks up a sack. In the sack is a bit of a bun.
Jack got up! He hops off the rock. He pecks at the bun in the sack.
Nick pats Jack on the back. Jack is a duck. Jack got his bun.

passage.title: The Chick in the Shed
paras: Chet has a shed at the back. In the shed is a hen. The hen has one thin chick.
The chick will not eat. Chet got a dish and put mash in it. He set the dish by the chick.
The chick did not wish to eat. It just sat in the sun and did not peck.
Then Chet got a thin chip of ham. He held it up. The chick ran to him and got it!
Now the chick will eat. Chet shuts the shed. He is much better at this than he was.

passage.title: The Fox in the Box
paras: Rex is a fox. Rex sits in a box at the back of the shed.
A quick bug got in the box. Rex did not want it in with him.
Rex got up. He did a quick dash at the bug.
The bug ran. Rex ran. The box tips on its top.
Now Rex has no box. He sits in a sack. Rex is a fox in a sack.

passage.title: The Bell on the Hill
paras: Nell has a job. The bell on the hill is hers. When it is six, Nell will hit the bell and the kids run up the path.
Then the bell fell off. It fell in the mud at the back of the mill. Nell did not yell.
She got a rag and a tub of suds. She did wash the bell until it was much bell and less mud.
Then Nell put the bell back on top of the hill. It was a big job.
At six, Nell hit the bell. The kids ran up the path. Nell will not miss.

passage.title: The Cave by the Lake
paras: Jane and Dave ride bikes to the lake. A cave is cut in the side of the hill. It is wide but it is not big.
Jane came up to the cave. She made a note of the time. Dave gave her a rope to hold.
Inside, Jane came to a pile of five white bones. A mole had made a home in the cave.
Jane did not take the bones. She made a note and came back out to Dave.
At home, Jane made a page in her log. She gave the cave a name. It is Mole Cave.

passage.title: The Frog Jump
paras: Fran has a frog. The frog is Spot. Spot can jump up on a stump.
The class had a frog jump. Ten frogs sat on a flat rock in the grass.
Stan had a frog that went fast. It went past Spot in one jump.
Then Spot bent his legs. He made a big jump and went past Stan's frog.
Spot won the frog jump. Fran held him up. The class clapped and Spot sat still.

passage.title: Six Hats
paras: Mom has six hats. The hats sit on a shelf in the hall.
Jen picks a hat. It flops on her nose. She can not see.
Dad grabs the next hat. It fits on him, but it is red with dots.
The pups get the last hat. They drag it to the rug and sit on it.
Mom gets the hat back. She puts the hats on the shelf. Then she picks the red one with dots.

passage.title: Ben's Bike
paras: Ben's bike is red. It has a bell and a big back rack.
Ben's dad fits a lamp on the front. Now Ben can ride when it is dim.
Ben rings the bell at the top of the lane. His pal Tess runs out.
Tess's bike is black. The two bikes go fast down the lane.
At the end they stop. Ben's hands are cold, but Ben's grin is big.

passage.title: The Picnic Basket
paras: Mom packs a basket. In it is a muffin, a napkin, and a bit of ham.
We walk to the sunset spot. Dad lugs the basket up the hill.
A rabbit sits in the grass. It is not upset. It just sits and blinks at us.
We sit on a blanket and eat. The muffin is the best bit.
The sun drops. We pack up the basket and walk back in the dim.

passage.title: The Cupcake Contest
paras: Our class has a cupcake contest. One kid, one cupcake.
Mandy makes a cupcake with a lime on top. It is bumpy but it smells fine.
Hudson makes one that is the size of his fist. He had to use a big pan.
Miss Hopkins picks Mandy's lime cupcake. Mandy did not expect it at all.
Mandy cuts it up so that the whole class can taste it. That was the best bit.

passage.title: Unpack the Van
paras: We are at the camp. Dad tells us to unpack the van.
I undo the straps. Ross unpacks the tent and the pots.
The tent is a mess. It is unfit for a dog, said Ross.
We unfold it on the grass. Bit by bit it stands up.
It is not a bad tent. It was just unpacked in a rush.

passage.title: The Pink Ring
paras: Gran has a pink ring. She puts it in a tin on the sink.
One time the ring is not in the tin. Gran thinks and thinks.
I check the sink. I check under the rug. No ring.
Then a clink! The ring is stuck in the sink, and it winks up at me.
Gran thanks me. She puts the ring back in the tin and we both sing.

passage.title: Why the Puppy Cried
paras: My puppy is Sky. She is shy and very funny.
Sky cried and cried. I did not know why.
Mom let me try to help. I gave Sky a dry rag and a bit of jelly on a dish.
Sky did not want it. Then I spot a tiny bit of glass stuck in her leg. I got it out.
Now Sky is happy. She can run and she does not cry.

passage.title: The Pitcher and the Catch
paras: Mitch is the pitcher. He can pitch a fast ball at the kids on his block.
Jack steps up with the bat. He swings and misses. Then he swings again.
Crack! The ball goes up and up. Mitch watches it drop.
Patch the dog runs and makes the catch. He will not let it go.
The kids yell. Patch gets a pat and the ball gets a bit of dog spit on it.

passage.title: The Storm in the Barn
paras: A storm hits the farm. The sky is dark and the wind is sharp.
Mark runs to the barn to shut it up. The corn in the cart is getting wet.
In the dark a short bark starts up. A pup is stuck under the cart.
Mark lifts the cart and the pup darts out. It is not hurt, just cross.
They sit in the barn until the storm stops. Then they walk back in the yard.

passage.title: Rain on Game Day
paras: Gail and Ray play on the same side. The big game was set for Saturday.
Then the rain came. It fell all day and it did not stay away.
The field was wet. The trail to it was just mud. Will the game wait?
Gail got a rake. Ray got a bag of sand. They did not wait for help. They made a dry way to the field.
At ten the sun came up and the game was on. Gail and Ray had mud on them, but they did play.

passage.title: The Seed Team
paras: Dean and Lee had a tray of seeds. They put each seed in a pot of dirt.
Each day they gave them a drink. The seeds did not seem to get big.
Lee said, “We need heat.” They set the pots near the glass where the sun is.
In a week, green leaves came up. Dean and Lee were pleased.
They had a real team of plants. Each pot got a name on a bit of tape.

passage.title: The Slow Boat
paras: Joan has a boat. It is slow. It will not go fast, and Joan likes it that way.
She rows down the stream. A crow sits on the bow and will not go.
By the road Joan sees a goat. The goat has its coat in a bush and is stuck.
Joan rows to the bank. She gets the coat free and the goat runs up the slope.
The crow stays all the way back. Joan said that crow may own the boat by now.

passage.title: The Gold Colt
paras: Old Mr Finch has a colt. The colt is gold and very bold.
It gets cold at dark. Mr Finch is told to hold the colt in the barn.
But the colt will not stay. It kicks the bolt and gets out in the wild grass.
We find it behind the post by the road. It is cold but it does not mind.
Mr Finch is kind. He folds a blanket on the colt and holds the rope all the way home.

passage.title: The Knot in the Night
paras: Dwight has a kite. The string has a knot in it that he can not undo.
He sits in the light by the window and tries. His knee is sore.
Mom knows how. She has a knack with string. She takes it and twists it right.
The knot comes undone. Dwight writes his name on the kite in black.
At night he hangs it high on the wall so he can see it from his bed.

passage.title: The Owl in the Woods
paras: We found an owl in the woods behind our house. It was on a low branch and would not move.
Mom said to stay back. An owl can look sound but still be hurt.
We counted out loud. One, two, three. The owl did not blink.
Then it took off without a sound and went up over the trees.
We stood and looked at the empty branch for a good long moment.

passage.title: The Berry Jar
paras: Perry has a berry bush by the shed. In the summer it is full of berries.
He fills a jar and carries it in. His mum is glad.
They stir the berries in a pan on the stove. The kitchen smells sweet.
Perry is sorry when the jar is done. He wants more.
Mum said there will be more next year. The bush is still there.

passage.title: The Pumpkin Contest
paras: The children in our street plant pumpkins every year.
My pumpkin is a monster. It took three of us to lift it onto the wagon.
Hamish has one that is small but perfect. It has no marks on it at all.
The teachers give the prize to Hamish. I am not upset. My pumpkin is still the biggest.
We take them both inside and make soup, and there is a lot for the whole street.

passage.title: The Helpful List
paras: Dad was restless. The shed was a mess and he did not know where to start.
I made him a list. It was short and it was helpful.
Sweep the floor. Sort the nails. Hang the tools on the wall.
He worked slowly and he worked gladly. By lunch the shed was spotless.
Dad said my list was the best thing in it. I felt useful all day.

passage.title: The Fastest Runner
paras: Last week our class was running races on the grass.
Bess is the fastest runner in the class. She has been winning since the first week.
But this time she was limping. She had twisted her leg the day before.
She ran anyway. She came in third and she was smiling the whole way.
The smallest kid in the class won. Bess clapped the hardest of all of us.

passage.title: The Misplaced Postcard
paras: Gran sent me a postcard from the sea. It never came.
She was upset. She had written it on the first day and posted it the same morning.
Three weeks later it turned up. It had been misplaced in the sorting room.
The postmark was blurred and one corner was bent, but I could read every word.
I have it on my wall now. It was worth the wait.

passage.title: Hopping to the Finish
paras: Our school had a hopping race on sports day.
You had to hop the whole way on one leg. Stopping meant starting again.
Robbie was winning. Then he got the giggles and fell sideways in the grass.
He got up and kept hopping. He was grinning the whole time.
He came last, and he was the only one still hopping at the end.

passage.title: The Giant of the Village
paras: In the centre of our village there is a huge stone giant.
The story says he was kind. He carried the stones for the arch on his own.
The city sent men to help, but by the time they came the arch was finished.
Once a year we place a ring of lamps round the giant.
My gran says the giant is a nice story. I think a nice story can still be real.

passage.title: The Badger at the Edge
paras: There is a badger that lives at the edge of our garden, under the hedge.
We never see it. We only see the ridge of earth it pushes up each night.
Dad put a camera by the bridge over the ditch to catch it.
For six nights there was nothing. On the seventh the badger walked straight past the lens.
We have the picture on the fridge now. It is not a good picture. We do not care.

passage.title: The Robot in the Basement
paras: Our friend Sam made a robot in his basement. He began it in April.
It has a motor, a silver body, and a tiny radio inside its head.
It cannot walk. It can only spin slowly on the spot and hum.
I think it is the finest thing I have ever seen. Sam does not think so.
He says a robot that only spins is a lamp. I say it is a robot that likes to dance.

passage.title: The Noise in the Attic
paras: There was a noise in the attic all the fall. A scratching, and then a pause.
Mum said it was the house settling. Dad said it was a bird.
I was wrong about it. I had heard a small voice up there.
In October we found them: four kittens in a box of straw, and a thin grey cat guarding the lot.
They live in the kitchen now. Nobody mentions the house settling any more.

passage.title: Making the Model
paras: Our class is making a model of the village out of card.
I am sticking the roofs on. Tam is shaping the trees.
We kept losing the small pieces, so we began using a lid to hold them.
By Friday the whole thing is standing, and it is hiding nothing. Every house is there.
We are taking it to the hall on Monday so the school can see it.

passage.title: The Happiest Day
paras: Last summer was the hottest we have had, and the days were the longest too.
We carried water to the garden every evening and studied the sky for rain.
None came. The grass dried and the leaves curled and nothing in the beds got any taller.
Then one Friday the sky went grey and it rained for an hour.
We stood out in it and got soaked, and it was the happiest I have been in a garden.

passage.title: The Robin and the Shed
paras: A robin made a nest on the shelf in our shed in April.
We could not finish the painting. We could not even open the door properly.
Dad put a wedge under it so the gap stayed the same all month.
The robin did not seem to mind us at all. It came and went past our heads.
By June the young had gone. We finished the shed in one afternoon.

passage.title: The Wobbly Table
paras: The table in our kitchen is terrible. One leg is shorter than the other three.
It wobbles whenever anybody puts an elbow on it. Every bottle falls over.
Gran folded a little piece of cardboard and pushed it under the short leg.
The wobble stopped at once. It was that simple.
Dad had been planning to buy a new table for a year. He is a bit annoyed.

passage.title: A Banana for the Walk
paras: We were about to set off on a long walk along the canal.
Mum gave us each a banana and a bottle of water to carry.
Ahead of us the path went away into the trees and we could not see the end of it.
An hour along, my brother sat down on a wall and ate his banana in about four bites.
Mine lasted the whole way. I am aware that this was the only part of the walk I won.

passage.title: She Won't Say Why
paras: My sister won't tell me where she goes on Saturday mornings.
She isn't rude about it. She just says, “You'll find out,” and gets her coat.
I don't like not knowing. I've tried asking Mum, who won't say.
Last week I followed her. She's been helping at the animal shelter since March.
She didn't mind me knowing. She said, “I'd have told you. You'd have wanted to come.”

passage.title: The Station Question
paras: Our station is tiny. One platform, one bench, and a sign with no information on it.
The six o'clock train had not come. There was no explanation and nobody to ask.
A man in a grey coat said it was cancelled. He gave no reason for that opinion.
Then the station master came out and said there was a problem with a signal.
The train came at seven. The man in the grey coat said he had known all along.

passage.title: The Artist on the Corner
paras: There is an artist who works on the corner by the market every Sunday.
She is incredibly fast. A whole street appears on her paper in about ten minutes.
Some stop and watch. Most of them are too shy to say anything.
I asked her once if drawing was teachable. She said it was, but patience was not.
I have been going back every Sunday since. I am slow, but I am not giving up.

passage.title: The Rematch
paras: Our team lost the first match by six goals. We had not prepared at all.
The coach did not shout. He proposed a rematch and set out a plan.
For three weeks we trained. We repeated the same drills until we did not have to think.
The rematch was in May. We did not win, but we only lost by one.
The coach said that was the best result he had ever seen from a defeat.

passage.title: The Report on the Volcano
paras: Our class had to write a report. I picked a volcano in Iceland.
I found a description of the last eruption in a library book.
It said the ash disrupted every flight in that part of the world for a week.
I wrote four sections and sketched the shape of the mountain in the margin.
My teacher said the drawing was not required but she was glad it was there.

passage.title: The Inspector and the Bridge
paras: An inspector came to look at the bridge over the river last spring.
She had to inspect every part of the structure, even the ones nobody can see.
She found a crack in one support. It was small, but it would not have stayed small.
The council had to reject her first plan because it cost too much.
In the end they fixed it properly. The bridge will stand for another hundred years.

passage.title: The Conductor's Visit
paras: A conductor visited our school in March to lead the orchestra for a day.
She was not what we had expected. She spoke quietly and watched everything.
She made us play one bar over and over until it was not a mess.
Then she made us play the whole piece, and that was not a mess at all.
I had never understood what a conductor was for. I do now.

passage.title: The Transport Museum
paras: The transport museum is enormous. It takes a whole day to walk round it.
There is a tram from 1902 that you can sit in. The seats are wooden and hard.
My favourite is the mail van. It is marvellous inside, with little shelves everywhere.
The guide was generous with her time. She let us ask questions until the bell went.
We are going back in October. It is the one trip nobody complains about.

passage.title: The Quiet Poet
paras: There is a poet who lives in the house at the end of our road.
She is very quiet. She does not create a fuss about anything.
Once a year she reads her poems in the hall by the science block.
The room is always full. People come from three villages to sit on hard chairs.
She never explains a poem. She says the poem has already done that.

passage.title: Eight Days of Rain
paras: It rained for eight days without stopping. The weight of the water bent the fence.
Our neighbour built a small wall of sandbags across the end of the drive.
On the eighth night the river came up and stopped two feet from the door.
In the morning the sky was blue, as though nothing had happened.
We spent a week clearing the field. The fruit trees had survived, which was the main thing.

passage.title: The Impossible Shelf
paras: Dad said the shelf would be impossible to put up without help. He was incorrect.
I measured the wall twice and marked it in pencil. It was not complicated.
The first hole was imperfect. I filled it and moved along two inches.
The second one was fine. The shelf went up and it is completely level.
Dad has not commented on it. He has put three books on it, which is a kind of comment.

passage.title: The Musician Next Door
paras: A musician moved in next door in the spring. She practises every day at six.
At first we were suspicious. Nobody wants an hour of scales from the next room.
But she is an exceptional player, and the sound is delicious rather than annoying.
My mother, who is cautious about everybody, now leaves her windows open on purpose.
It is official. We are the only street in town with free music every evening.

passage.title: Admitted and Forgotten
paras: I had been forgetting things all term. I admitted it to my teacher in November.
She was not upset. She said the beginning of a fix is noticing.
We set up a system. Everything I was committing to went straight in one notebook.
By the end of term I had not forgotten a single thing. I was quite surprised.
She said the notebook was not magic. She said I had simply stopped relying on luck.

passage.title: The Elephant Photograph
paras: There is a photograph of an elephant on the wall of our school hall.
My grandfather took it. He was a photographer for a newspaper for thirty years.
The elephant is standing in a river with its trunk up, and the light is orange.
People stop in front of it every day. Nobody ever walks straight past.
I like that a photograph taken before I was born can still stop a person in a corridor.

passage.title: The Myth in the Gym
paras: There is a myth in our school that the gym was built on top of an old well.
Every pupil hears it in the first week. Nobody has ever checked it.
Last year a system of cracks appeared across one corner of the floor.
The caretaker lifted a board. There was no well. There was a very old pipe.
The myth has not changed at all. People still tell it, and they tell it better now.

passage.title: The Rhino in Autumn
paras: The rhino at the wildlife park has a name but nobody uses it.
In autumn she stands by the fence for hours and watches the leaves come down.
The keeper says it is not a mystery. She likes movement, and leaves move.
There is a rhythm to it. A leaf falls, she turns her head, she waits for the next one.
I could watch her do that all day. I am told that I have.

passage.title: The Telescope on the Roof
paras: My aunt is a biologist, but her real passion is the telescope on her roof.
She built the platform herself and photographs the sky from it on clear nights.
She has a catalogue of every photograph, organised by date and by what is in it.
She let me look through it once at Saturn. I did not say anything for a while.
She said that was the correct response and made me a cup of tea.

passage.title: The Antique Machine
paras: There is an antique machine in the window of the shop on the corner.
It is unique. The man in the shop says there is no other one like it in the country.
It has a brass plaque on the side with a date and a name in French.
Nobody knows what it was for. The chef next door thinks it made chocolate.
I hope nobody ever finds out. It is better as a question.

passage.title: A Month of Mondays
paras: One month last winter, something went wrong with every single Monday.
The oven broke. The front door stuck. My brother lost a glove, twice.
My mother started to wonder whether we should simply skip Mondays altogether.
Then one Monday nothing happened at all. We came home and sat down and nothing broke.
We talked about that quiet Monday for weeks. It was the best one we had.

passage.title: Worth the Work
paras: My grandmother worked the same patch of ground for forty years.
She says the first word of gardening is patience and the second is work.
Nothing in that garden arrived quickly. The apple tree took nine years to fruit.
She never once said it was not worth it. Not in all the time I knew her.
The tree is still there. Every autumn the whole world seems to come and pick from it.

passage.title: The Performance
paras: Our class gave a performance in the village hall at the end of the year.
There was a long silence before it started. The audience was patient.
My part was small, but the difference between knowing it and not knowing it was everything.
The applause at the end went on for ages. My father stood up, which was embarrassing.
On the way home nobody mentioned the mistakes. There had been several.

passage.title: The Thing I Was Taught
paras: My uncle taught me to fish when I was eight. It was the only thing he ever taught me.
We caught nothing at all for three whole days. I thought about giving up.
He said he had brought me here to learn to wait, not to learn to catch.
On the fourth day I caught one. It was small and I put it back.
I have thought about what he said far more often than I have fished.
